ga-luoc-tien-yen-quang-ninh.name: Tiên Yên boiled chicken
aliases: Boiled Tiên Yên hill chicken with lime leaf
ga-luoc-tien-yen-quang-ninh.serving_basis: One chicken weighing about 1.4 kg, cut into 8–10 pieces and shared by four people.
ga-luoc-tien-yen-quang-ninh.description: Tiên Yên chicken is known for fragrant, sweet meat, a firm bite and naturally golden skin. Bếp Việt keeps the preparation simple so the chicken remains the focus, adding a little ginger, shallot and lime leaf. Serve warm with lime-pepper salt or ginger dipping sauce.
ga-luoc-tien-yen-quang-ninh.finished_dish: The chicken is just cooked, with moist, firm white meat and glossy golden skin; cut into serving pieces and finish with finely sliced lime leaf and lime-pepper salt.
ga-luoc-tien-yen-quang-ninh.serving: Let the chicken rest briefly, cut through the joints and arrange on a platter with lime leaf. Serve warm with salt, pepper and lime; the cooking broth can be seasoned and served as soup.
tips: Choose traceable Tiên Yên chicken. If it is unavailable, use a similarly sized free-range chicken to keep a firm texture.
Keep the pot at a gentle simmer rather than a rolling boil so the skin is less likely to split and the meat cooks evenly. Timing depends on the bird's size and age.
Use a food thermometer to check that the thickest part of the thigh reaches at least 74°C. Rest the chicken in the hot broth for about 10 minutes before cutting.
ga-luoc-tien-yen-quang-ninh.image_alt: Tiên Yên boiled chicken with naturally golden skin, cut into pieces and served with lime leaf and a small bowl of lime-pepper salt; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
ga-luoc-tien-yen-quang-ninh.time_note: About 1 hour 15 minutes, including 45 minutes of simmering and a 10-minute rest; timing depends on the chicken's size.

ingredients.name: Cleaned Tiên Yên chicken
ingredients.notes: Choose traceable poultry and keep it whole for boiling.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Use a pot deep enough to mostly cover the chicken.

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger
ingredients.notes: Rinse and crush.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peel and crush.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the cooking water; adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Lime leaves
ingredients.notes: Add some to the pot and finely slice the rest for serving.

ingredients.name: Coarse salt
ingredients.notes: For the dipping salt.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: For the dipping salt.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: Add to the salt and pepper at the end.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Optional; mince for the dipping salt.

preparation_steps: Check the cavity and remove any uncleaned giblets. Rinse the chicken under clean running water and pat dry. Keep raw poultry away from ready-to-eat foods and clean the sink after preparation.
Crush the ginger and shallot and rinse the lime leaves. Mix coarse salt with pepper and lime juice; add minced chili if desired.
cooking_steps: Put the water, ginger, shallot and salt in a deep pot. Bring to a boil, lower to a gentle simmer and carefully add the chicken.
Simmer for about 35–45 minutes depending on size, turning the chicken once. Use a food thermometer to check that the thickest part of the thigh reaches at least 74°C; do not rely on skin color alone.
Turn off the heat, cover and let the chicken rest in the hot water for 10 minutes. Lift it out to drain, rest briefly, then cut through the joints and finish with finely sliced lime leaf.
Serve warm with lime-pepper salt. Strain and season the cooking broth as soup if desired.

banh-tet-la-cam-can-tho.name: Cần Thơ magenta-leaf bánh tét
aliases: Purple bánh tét from Cần Thơ
Magenta-leaf bánh tét with pork and salted egg
banh-tet-la-cam-can-tho.serving_basis: One medium roll, cut into about 16 slices; serve two slices per person as a main or side.
banh-tet-la-cam-can-tho.description: Bình Thủy bánh tét lá cẩm has naturally purple sticky rice wrapped around mung beans, pork and salted duck egg yolk. Bếp Việt adapts a one-roll family batch, coloring the rice with magenta-leaf infusion, mixing it with coconut milk, then wrapping it in banana leaves and simmering until fully cooked.
banh-tet-la-cam-can-tho.finished_dish: Each slice has a chewy violet rice layer around yellow mung beans, tender pork and salted egg yolk; the cross-section is round and holds together without becoming mushy.
banh-tet-la-cam-can-tho.serving: Let the roll cool slightly, then use a sharp knife to cut slices about 1.5 cm thick. Serve as a light meal or pan-sear both sides for a fragrant, lightly crisp surface.
tips: Soak the rice in strained magenta-leaf water for an even color; drain it thoroughly before mixing in coconut milk.
Wrap firmly but leave room for the rice to expand. Seal the banana-leaf ends so cooking water does not enter the filling.
Keep the roll submerged throughout boiling and top up with hot water. Cool leftovers promptly and refrigerate.
search_terms: bánh tét with pork and salted egg
banh-tet-la-cam-can-tho.image_alt: Cần Thơ magenta-leaf bánh tét with violet rice, mung bean, pork and salted egg filling, sliced on a plate; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
banh-tet-la-cam-can-tho.time_note: About 9 hours 30 minutes, including 4 hours of rice soaking and 4 hours 30 minutes of boiling; soak the rice overnight if convenient.

ingredients.name: Glutinous rice
ingredients.notes: Rinse, soak in magenta-leaf infusion for 3–4 hours and drain.

ingredients.name: Fresh magenta leaves
ingredients.notes: Rinse, simmer to make purple cooking water and strain.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For the leaf infusion and soaking the rice.

ingredients.name: Coconut milk
ingredients.notes: Mix into the soaked and drained rice.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Divide between the rice and filling.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Lightly season the rice.

ingredients.name: Split mung beans
ingredients.notes: Soak for two hours and steam until soft.

ingredients.name: Pork belly
ingredients.notes: Cut into long strips the length of the roll.

ingredients.name: Salted duck egg yolks
ingredients.notes: Rinse and pat dry; place lengthwise in the filling.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Mince for the pork filling.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season the pork; adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: Season the pork filling.

ingredients.name: Banana leaves
ingredients.notes: Wipe clean and briefly soften over heat; use intact leaves.

ingredients.name: Food-safe tying string
ingredients.notes: Tie the roll securely.

preparation_steps: Rinse and lightly crush the magenta leaves. Simmer them in water for 15 minutes until the liquid is deep purple, strain out the leaves and cool. Rinse the rice, soak it in the infusion for 3–4 hours, then drain thoroughly.
Soak the mung beans for two hours, steam until soft and mash coarsely. Season the pork with shallot, fish sauce, pepper and some of the salt; pan-cook until browned and cooked through.
Soften and dry the banana leaves. Mix the drained rice with coconut milk, sugar and the remaining salt; set out the beans, pork and salted egg yolks for wrapping.
cooking_steps: Lay several banana leaves in overlapping layers. Spread rice, add mung beans, pork and egg yolk in the center, then cover with rice. Roll tightly into a cylinder, fold the ends and tie evenly.
Line a large pot with banana leaves, add the roll and cover with boiling water. Simmer for about 4–4.5 hours, checking often and adding boiling water to keep the roll submerged.
Lift out the roll, briefly rinse the leaf exterior with clean water and hang or tilt it to drain. Let it cool and set before removing the ties and slicing with a clean knife.

banh-trang-phoi-suong-trang-bang.name: Trảng Bàng dew-wetted rice paper rolls with boiled pork
aliases: Trảng Bàng rice paper rolls with pork
banh-trang-phoi-suong-trang-bang.serving_basis: About 16 medium rolls, served as a shared main meal for four.
banh-trang-phoi-suong-trang-bang.description: Trảng Bàng's signature rolls pair soft, pliable dew-wetted rice paper with boiled pork, fresh rice vermicelli and a generous selection of greens, especially local forest herbs. Bếp Việt adapts an easy home platter with familiar herbs and pineapple fermented-fish sauce for a savory, fresh balance.
banh-trang-phoi-suong-trang-bang.finished_dish: Pliable rice paper wraps boiled pork, vermicelli and greens without tearing; serve with pineapple fermented-fish sauce balanced between salty, sweet and sour.
banh-trang-phoi-suong-trang-bang.serving: Arrange the rice paper, pork, vermicelli, herbs and vegetables separately so everyone can roll their own. Dew-wetted rice paper is usually ready to use without dipping in water.
tips: Do not soak pliable dew-wetted rice paper. Keep unused sheets covered so they do not dry out.
Start the pork in cold water for even cooking. Check the thickest piece with a food thermometer; it should reach at least 71°C before slicing.
Wash the greens thoroughly under clean running water and drain well. Add fermented-fish sauce gradually because saltiness varies by brand.
search_terms: Tây Ninh rice paper and forest herbs
banh-trang-phoi-suong-trang-bang.image_alt: Trảng Bàng dew-wetted rice paper rolls with boiled pork, vermicelli, herbs and cucumber, served with fermented-fish sauce; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
banh-trang-phoi-suong-trang-bang.time_note: About 55 minutes to prepare the greens, boil the pork and make the dipping sauce; assemble the rolls at the table.

ingredients.name: Trảng Bàng dew-wetted rice paper
ingredients.notes: Choose pliable, intact sheets; they usually do not need to be dipped in water.

ingredients.name: Pork belly
ingredients.notes: Choose a piece with balanced meat and fat and rinse it clean.

ingredients.name: Fresh rice vermicelli
ingredients.notes: Briefly blanch if needed and drain.

ingredients.name: Fresh greens and herbs
ingredients.notes: Use lettuce, perilla, basil, fish mint and seasonal forest herbs.

ingredients.name: Cucumber
ingredients.notes: Rinse and cut into long sticks.

ingredients.name: Pickled bean sprouts
ingredients.notes: Drain well; lightly pickled vegetables also work.

ingredients.name: Fermented anchovy sauce
ingredients.notes: Use a dipping-sauce variety and adjust to its saltiness.

ingredients.name: Pineapple
ingredients.notes: Finely chop half; juice the rest if desired.

ingredients.name: Warm water
ingredients.notes: Dilute the sauce if needed.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Season the sauce, adjusting for the sweetness of the pineapple.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Optional; mince.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Crush and add to the pork cooking water.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season the pork cooking water.

preparation_steps: Wash the greens several times under clean running water and drain completely. Cut the cucumber and arrange the vermicelli, pickled vegetables and rice paper separately on a platter.
Rinse the pork and place it in a pot of cold water with crushed ginger and salt. Mince the pineapple, garlic and chili; set out the fermented-fish sauce, sugar and warm water.
cooking_steps: Bring the pork to a boil, skim the foam and lower the heat to a gentle simmer for about 20–25 minutes depending on thickness. Check that the center reaches at least 71°C with a food thermometer; cool before slicing thinly.
Combine fermented-fish sauce, chopped pineapple, garlic, sugar and warm water in a small saucepan. Simmer for 2–3 minutes until fragrant, taste and add chili; let it cool slightly before serving.
Arrange the rice paper, pork, vermicelli, herbs, cucumber and pickled vegetables on a platter. Roll each serving just before eating and dip in the sauce.

banh-beo-cam-kim-hoi-an.name: Cẩm Kim Hội An bánh bèo rice cakes
aliases: Quảng Nam bánh bèo with shrimp and pork
banh-beo-cam-kim-hoi-an.serving_basis: About 16 small bowls, four per person; serve hot with seasoned fish sauce.
banh-beo-cam-kim-hoi-an.description: Cẩm Kim bánh bèo is a rustic Hội An breakfast, prepared in the Quảng Nam style with thicker, soft rice cakes and a minced shrimp-and-pork topping. Bếp Việt adapts a family batch steamed in small bowls, finished with scallion oil and fried shallots and served with mildly spicy fish sauce.
banh-beo-cam-kim-hoi-an.finished_dish: Small bowls of opaque white rice cake with a soft, moderately thick texture, topped with orange-brown minced shrimp and pork, fried shallots and scallion oil; serve with fish sauce on the side or spooned over.
banh-beo-cam-kim-hoi-an.serving: Serve the cakes as soon as they come out of the steamer, topped with hot shrimp-and-pork mixture, scallion oil and fried shallots. Add a little fish sauce to each bowl or serve it on the side.
tips: Stir the batter again before pouring because rice flour settles. A moderate layer lets the cakes steam evenly in small bowls.
Preheat the empty bowls in the steamer so the batter sets smoothly; avoid opening the lid repeatedly while the cakes cook.
Season the Quảng Nam-style shrimp-and-pork topping lightly so the shrimp's sweetness remains clear; adjust the fish sauce at the table.
search_terms: bánh bèo with minced shrimp and pork
banh-beo-cam-kim-hoi-an.image_alt: Small bowls of Cẩm Kim Hội An bánh bèo topped with minced shrimp and pork, scallion oil and fried shallots on a ceramic tray; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
banh-beo-cam-kim-hoi-an.time_note: About 1 hour 10 minutes, including 20 minutes for the batter to rest and steaming in batches.

ingredients.name: Rice flour
ingredients.notes: Use fine white rice flour.

ingredients.name: Tapioca starch
ingredients.notes: Adds a light chew; use less for a softer cake.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Whisk into the flour gradually to prevent lumps.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Lightly season the batter.

ingredients.name: Peeled fresh shrimp
ingredients.notes: Remove the vein and mince.

ingredients.name: Pork shoulder
ingredients.notes: Mince finely and retain a little fat so the topping stays moist.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Mince for frying.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Finely slice for scallion oil.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Divide between the topping and scallion oil.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Divide between the topping and dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Divide between the topping and dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: For the dipping sauce; adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Optional; mince for the dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Fried shallots
ingredients.notes: Scatter over the cakes before serving.

preparation_steps: Whisk rice flour, tapioca starch, salt and water until smooth. Rest for 20 minutes, then stir again; prepare 16 clean small bowls and a steamer.
Mince the shrimp, pork and shallot. Slice the scallions. Mix fish sauce, sugar, lime juice, warm water and chili to taste for the dipping sauce.
cooking_steps: Set the empty bowls in the steamer to warm. Stir the batter, fill each bowl halfway to two-thirds and steam for 7–9 minutes until the cakes turn opaque and the surface is just set.

While the cakes steam, fry the shallot in some of the oil until fragrant. Add the pork and cook through, then add the shrimp and fish sauce; stir-fry until the topping is fully cooked and lightly moist.
Warm the remaining oil and pour it over the scallions. Spoon the topping onto each cake, add scallion oil and fried shallots, then serve hot with seasoned fish sauce.

canh-la-mi-ca-dang-ca-kho-tay-nguyen.name: Central Highlands cassava-leaf soup with bitter eggplant and dried fish
aliases: Cassava-leaf and bitter-eggplant soup with dried fish
canh-la-mi-ca-dang-ca-kho-tay-nguyen.serving_basis: About 1.4 liters of soup, divided among four bowls and served with steamed rice.
canh-la-mi-ca-dang-ca-kho-tay-nguyen.description: Cassava-leaf soup is an everyday forest-vegetable dish in many Central Highlands communities. Young cassava leaves are pounded and simmered with bitter eggplant and dried fish, creating a nutty, gently bitter flavor associated with the highlands. Bếp Việt adapts a home version and emphasizes careful processing of the leaves before they enter the pot.
canh-la-mi-ca-dang-ca-kho-tay-nguyen.finished_dish: Soft cassava leaves simmer in a green-brown broth with intact pieces of bitter eggplant and lightly smoky dried fish; the flavor is gently bitter, nutty and moderately salty.
canh-la-mi-ca-dang-ca-kho-tay-nguyen.serving: Ladle the soup hot into bowls and serve with steamed rice. Taste for salt only after the dried fish has released its flavor; serve fresh chili separately if desired.
tips: Use only young cassava leaves sold for food and process them safely; raw cassava leaves contain cyanogenic compounds.

Pound the leaves thoroughly for at least 10 minutes, wash them with plenty of clean water, boil separately for 8–10 minutes and discard all the cooking water. Then simmer them in the soup until very tender.
Dried fish is already salty, so rinse it briefly, toast it and add fish sauce only at the end. Reduce the bitter eggplant if diners are new to its flavor.
canh-la-mi-ca-dang-ca-kho-tay-nguyen.image_alt: A bowl of Central Highlands cassava-leaf soup with bitter eggplant and dried fish, the leaves tender in a green-brown broth; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
canh-la-mi-ca-dang-ca-kho-tay-nguyen.time_note: About 1 hour 5 minutes, including careful leaf preparation, a separate brief boil and a second simmer until fully tender.

ingredients.name: Young cassava leaves prepared as food
ingredients.notes: Use only food-grade young leaves; pound, wash, boil separately and discard that water before making the soup.

ingredients.name: Bitter eggplant
ingredients.notes: Rinse and halve larger fruits.

ingredients.name: Dried fish
ingredients.notes: Choose edible dried fish, rinse briefly and toast; check for bones before eating.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For the soup; use separate additional water to wash and boil the leaves, then discard it.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Crush and cut into pieces.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peel and crush.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Crush and add if desired.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Optional; omit for a more rustic preparation.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Add at the end because dried fish is salty.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Add only if the broth still needs seasoning.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Optional; slice and serve on the side.

preparation_steps: Pick young cassava leaves and remove tough stems. Pound thoroughly for at least 10 minutes, wash with plenty of clean water and change the water. Boil the leaves separately for 8–10 minutes and discard all of that water. Do not taste raw leaves or use leaves of uncertain origin.
Briefly rinse the dried fish, toast it and remove large bones. Rinse the bitter eggplant; crush the lemongrass, shallot and garlic.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and fry the shallot, garlic and lemongrass until fragrant. Add the dried fish and stir briefly to release its aroma.
Pour in the soup water and bring to a gentle boil. Add the pre-boiled, drained cassava leaves and bitter eggplant. Lower the heat and simmer for 20–25 minutes until the leaves are very soft.
Season with fish sauce and add salt only if needed. Simmer for a few more minutes, check that the leaves are fully tender and the eggplant is cooked, then serve hot with steamed rice.
